_comment: Toy corpus for the prior-art demo. Entirely fictional documents invented for teaching. Dates, numbers and text are made up; nothing here is a real patent. Structure mirrors what you would get from EPO OPS / PATSTAT: bibliographic data, dates, family id, CPC, and sectioned full text.

disclosure.title: Selective hydrogenation of an unsaturated aldehyde over a cerium-promoted palladium catalyst
disclosure.text: A process for the selective hydrogenation of an unsaturated aldehyde, wherein the catalyst comprises palladium supported on a gamma-alumina carrier, the catalyst further comprising cerium as a promoter in an amount of 0.4 to 0.6 wt%, the reaction being carried out at a temperature of 180 to 220 degrees C and at a hydrogen to substrate molar ratio of 2.2 to 2.4.

documents.title: Hydrogenation catalyst comprising palladium on an aluminium oxide carrier

sections.claims: 1. A hydrogenation catalyst comprising palladium deposited on a gamma-aluminium oxide carrier, characterised in that the catalyst further comprises lanthanum as a promoter in an amount of 1.0 to 5.0 wt%.
sections.description: The catalyst of the invention is prepared by impregnation of the gamma-aluminium oxide carrier with a palladium salt. Hydrogenation is conveniently carried out at a temperature of 150 to 200 degrees C.
sections.examples: Example 4: palladium (0.5 wt%) on gamma-aluminium oxide promoted with lanthanum (2.0 wt%), operated at 175 degrees C.

documents.title: Hydrogenation catalyst comprising palladium on an aluminium oxide carrier

sections.claims: 1. A hydrogenation catalyst comprising palladium deposited on a gamma-aluminium oxide carrier and lanthanum in an amount of 1.0 to 5.0 wt%.
sections.description: US member of the same family. Hydrogenation at 150 to 200 degrees C.
sections.examples: Example 4 as in the parent application.

documents.title: Process for hydrogenating aldehydes over supported noble metal catalysts

sections.claims: 1. A process for hydrogenating an unsaturated aldehyde in the presence of a palladium catalyst supported on activated carbon, at a temperature of 190 to 260 degrees C.
sections.description: The hydrogen to substrate molar ratio is maintained between 2.5 and 3.0 throughout the reaction.
sections.examples: Example 7: reaction at 210 degrees C with a hydrogen to substrate molar ratio of 2.8.

documents.title: Cerium-promoted nickel catalyst for selective hydrogenation

sections.claims: 1. A catalyst comprising nickel on a gamma-alumina support, the catalyst comprising cerium in an amount of 0.1 to 0.3 wt%.
sections.description: Selective hydrogenation is carried out at a temperature of 200 to 240 degrees C. The cerium promoter improves selectivity toward the unsaturated alcohol.
sections.examples: Example 2: nickel (5 wt%) with cerium (0.2 wt%) on gamma-alumina at 220 degrees C.

documents.title: Selective hydrogenation process with controlled hydrogen feed

sections.claims: 1. A hydrogenation process wherein a palladium catalyst on an Al2O3 carrier of the gamma phase is used, and wherein the hydrogen to substrate molar ratio is from 1.0 to 2.1.
sections.description: The reaction temperature is preferably from 170 to 210 degrees C. Controlling the hydrogen feed suppresses over-hydrogenation.

documents.title: Effect of cerium loading on palladium hydrogenation catalysts

sections.description: We report the effect of cerium loading on palladium catalysts supported on gamma-alumina. Loadings of 0.8 to 1.2 wt% cerium gave the highest selectivity in the hydrogenation of unsaturated aldehydes.
sections.examples: Catalysts were tested at 200 degrees C at a hydrogen to substrate molar ratio of 2.0.

documents.title: Promoted palladium catalyst and use thereof

sections.claims: 1. A catalyst comprising palladium on a gamma-alumina support and cerium in an amount of 0.35 to 0.75 wt%, used at a temperature of 175 to 225 degrees C.
sections.description: Filed before the disclosure's priority date but published afterwards. Under EPC Art. 54(3) such a document counts for novelty only, never for inventive step.
sections.examples: Example 3: cerium 0.5 wt% at 200 degrees C.

sections.claims: 1. A catalyst comprising palladium on gamma-alumina with cerium in an amount of 0.4 to 0.6 wt% at 180 to 220 degrees C.
sections.description: This document is filed AFTER the disclosure's priority date. It is not prior art at all, and a system that ignores dates would report it as a perfect anticipation.
sections.examples: Example 1: cerium 0.5 wt% at 200 degrees C, hydrogen to substrate molar ratio 2.3.

documents.title: Chelating agent for metal recovery from spent catalysts

sections.claims: 1. A method of recovering palladium from a spent catalyst using a chelating agent.
sections.description: The chelating agent is preferably ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid. Recovery is carried out at ambient temperature.
sections.examples: Example 1: leaching with EDTA at 25 degrees C.

sections.claims: 1. A reactor comprising structured packing for gas-liquid contacting.
sections.description: Suitable for hydrogenation service at elevated temperature. No catalyst composition is claimed.
sections.examples: Example 1: packing tested at 200 degrees C.

sections.claims: 1. A method of preparing a palladium catalyst on an aluminium oxide of the gamma phase carrier by impregnation.
sections.description: The prepared catalyst is used in hydrogenation at 160 to 230 degrees C. Machine translation from Chinese.
sections.examples: Example 5: impregnation followed by calcination at 450 degrees C.

sections.claims: 1. A catalyst comprising a noble metal and a rare-earth promoter on a refractory oxide support.
sections.description: Rare-earth promoters include cerium, lanthanum and praseodymium, typically at 1.5 to 8 wt%. The noble metal may be palladium or platinum.
sections.examples: Example 2: palladium with cerium at 3.0 wt% on alumina.

compound.name: rare-earth promoted noble metal on refractory oxide
